patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined in 2021. Endometriosis diagnosed clinically by gynecology in 2023 with a left endometrioma; laparoscopy declined; after a break the couple resumed trying in late 2024, and a 2026 infertility workup is normal, with a reproductive endocrinology referral open today.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called after school hours asking to establish with the practice. Teaches second grade locally, had been driving back to her old primary care office for appointments and would like someone closer. Membership agreement and welcome packet emailed. Records release for prior primary care office completed by e-signature, faxed today. New patient physical booked 10/5 at 7:30 am, before her school day. Asked her to come fasting.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o woman establishing care. Previously followed at a primary care office about an hour away; records requested.

No ongoing medical problems. Never hospitalized. No surgeries. No meds other than ibuprofen for period cramps, a day or two each cycle. NKDA.

GYN: menarche in her early teens, cycles regular about monthly, cramping usually the first day or two, manageable with OTC ibuprofen. No bleeding between periods. Married, one partner. Never had a pelvic infection or STI. Last Pap 2020 per patient, normal. Not currently trying to conceive; may in the next year or two.

Family: mother has endometriosis. Mother's sister had trouble getting pregnant. No known heart disease, diabetes or cancer in parents.

Social: teaches elementary school. Married. Never a smoker. Does not drink. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above. Mood good. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals per flowsheet, BMI about 22. HEENT clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin without concerning lesions. No edema. Pelvic not done today, Pap not due.

A/P: healthy adult, preventive care.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees.
- Flu vaccine given today. COVID primary series done in the spring per patient, card on file to be scanned with outside records.
- Tdap was within 10 years per her recollection; will confirm from records.
- Pap due 2023.
- Period cramps on ibuprofen as needed, fine for now; let me know if it changes.
- Return in a year, or sooner by text or call.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Melissa, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol are all in the normal range. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Good to have you with us.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received by fax, 23 pages, from her previous primary care office. Abstracted:
- Problem list: none active.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical cytology 07/2020: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Immunizations: Tdap 08/2017. COVID-19 Pfizer 03/27/2021 and 04/17/2021 (from scanned vaccination card).
- Last physical 07/2020, unremarkable.
Immunizations entered. Scanned to media. Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Question about summer camp form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm helping run the district's summer reading camp this year and they want a health form signed by a doctor. Do I need to come in or can I drop it off? Thanks, Melissa

documents.title: Re: Question about summer camp form
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Melissa, you were just seen in October, so you can upload it here or drop it at the front desk. Doctor will sign and we'll message you when it's ready, usually within two business days.

documents.title: Annual visit reminder
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Melissa, it's time to schedule your yearly physical. Flu and COVID boosters for this season are in stock and can be given at the same visit. Reply with a few early mornings that suit you.

documents.title: Re: Annual visit reminder
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Any morning the week of Oct 10 before 8 works. Thank you!

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing well. School year off to a busy start.

Interval: no illnesses, no ED or urgent care. Still uses ibuprofen for cramps at the start of each period; says they have been a bit worse over the past year or so but still manageable, does not miss work. Cycles regular. No bleeding between periods.

She and her husband are planning to start trying for a pregnancy this fall. Asked what she should do beforehand. Talked through: keep up with vaccines (flu and COVID today, both fine before and during pregnancy), and she already avoids alcohol and tobacco. Advised to call when she has a positive test so we can get her connected with obstetrics. Mother's history of endometriosis and aunt's infertility noted again; nothing to do about it now unless trying takes longer than expected, in which case she should tell us.

Meds: none. NKDA.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 22. Well-appearing. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P: healthy, planning pregnancy. Vaccines given. Pap due next year. Labs from last fall were normal; none today. Annual next fall.
